exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 Choosing a Festival to Visit
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Lucy
transcript.text: We have a free week in spring. Which festival should we travel to see?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I'd love to see the Rio Carnival. The dancing and music look so exciting.

transcript.speaker: Lucy
transcript.text: It does look amazing, but it's very far away and the weather is so hot.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Good point. What would you prefer then?

transcript.speaker: Lucy
transcript.text: I'd rather visit the Lantern Festival. I love guessing riddles and seeing the lights.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: That sounds relaxing. And the floating lanterns on the river must be beautiful.

transcript.speaker: Lucy
transcript.text: Exactly. Let's choose the Lantern Festival this time and save the carnival for later.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Agreed. I'll start planning our trip tonight.

exercises.translation_cn: Lucy 和 Tom 商量春天去看哪个节日;Tom 想去里约狂欢节,觉得歌舞很刺激;但 Lucy 嫌太远又太热;她更想去元宵节,喜欢猜灯谜和看灯;Tom 觉得轻松,河上漂浮的灯笼一定很美;两人决定这次去元宵节,把狂欢节留到以后。

Why does Lucy worry about that choice?
options: It is far away and the weather is hot.

options: Guessing riddles and seeing the lights.

questions.stem: What does Tom say about the river at the festival?
options: The floating lanterns must be beautiful.

questions.stem: What do they finally decide?
options: To go to the carnival now.
To visit the Lantern Festival this time.

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 The Story of Halloween
exercises.speaker: uk_female
exercises.transcript: Halloween is celebrated on the last day of October. Although it began with religious origins long ago, it has slowly become an exciting festival, especially for children. On this night, children dress up in funny or frightening costumes and go from house to house asking for sweets. People carve faces into large orange pumpkins and place lights inside them. Some families decorate their homes and tell scary stories in the dark. The festival is no longer about its old religious meaning; today it is mostly about having fun together. For many children, it is one of the most enjoyable nights of the whole year.
exercises.translation_cn: 万圣节在10月最后一天庆祝;虽然很久以前源于宗教,但如今已渐渐变成一个有趣的节日,尤其受孩子喜爱;这一夜孩子们打扮成搞笑或吓人的样子,挨家挨户讨糖;人们在橙色大南瓜上刻脸并放灯;有些家庭装饰房屋、在黑暗中讲恐怖故事;如今它已不再关乎旧的宗教含义,而主要是大家一起玩乐;对许多孩子来说,这是一年中最快乐的夜晚之一。

questions.stem: When is Halloween celebrated?
options: On the last day of October.

questions.stem: How has Halloween changed over time?
options: It has become a fun festival, especially for children.
It has become a quiet religious day.

questions.stem: What do children do on Halloween night?
options: They dress up and ask for sweets from house to house.

questions.stem: What do people do with pumpkins?
options: They carve faces into them and put lights inside.
They sell them at a fair.

questions.stem: What is Halloween mostly about today?

exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 At the Carnival
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Reporter
transcript.text: Excuse me, you're wearing such a bright costume. Are you enjoying the carnival?

transcript.speaker: Maria
transcript.text: Oh yes! It's the most exciting day of my whole year.

transcript.speaker: Reporter
transcript.text: How long did it take to prepare your costume?

transcript.speaker: Maria
transcript.text: Months! My friends and I worked on it for nearly a year.

transcript.speaker: Reporter
transcript.text: That's amazing. What's your favourite part of the carnival?

transcript.speaker: Maria
transcript.text: Marching along the streets while everyone dances to the samba music.

transcript.speaker: Reporter
transcript.text: And how do you feel right now, in the middle of the crowd?

transcript.speaker: Maria
transcript.text: I feel free and full of joy. There's nothing else like it!

exercises.translation_cn: 记者采访身穿亮丽服装的 Maria 是否享受狂欢节;Maria 说这是她一年中最激动的一天;服装准备了好几个月,和朋友们做了近一年;她最喜欢的是在桑巴音乐中沿街游行;此刻置身人群中,她感到自由、满心喜悦,觉得没有什么能与之相比。

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 Mongolian Wrestling
exercises.speaker: uk_female
exercises.transcript: Wrestling is one of the most important events at the Naadam Festival. Mongolian wrestling is quite different from the wrestling you see at the Olympic Games. There are no rounds, and the wrestlers are not separated by weight, so a smaller man may face a much larger one. A wrestler loses the match as soon as any part of his body above the knee touches the ground. Before each match, the competitors dance onto the field, waving their arms as if they were eagles. Watching their strength and grace, many visitors feel deeply moved. For the Mongolian people, wrestling is far more than a sport; it is a proud part of their culture.
exercises.translation_cn: 摔跤是那达慕节最重要的项目之一;蒙古摔跤与奥运会的摔跤很不一样;没有回合,也不按体重分级,所以小个子可能对上大块头;一旦膝盖以上的任何部位触地,摔跤手就算输;每场比赛前,选手们像雄鹰一样挥臂舞入场地;看着他们的力量与优雅,许多游客深受感动;对蒙古人来说,摔跤远不只是一项运动,而是他们文化中令人自豪的一部分。

questions.stem: How is Mongolian wrestling different from Olympic wrestling?
options: It is played with a ball.
It has no rounds and no weight classes.

questions.stem: When does a wrestler lose the match?
options: When a part of his body above the knee touches the ground.

options: They dance onto the field, waving their arms like eagles.

questions.stem: How do many visitors feel while watching?
options: Deeply moved by the strength and grace.

questions.stem: What does wrestling mean to the Mongolian people?

exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 Thanksgiving Abroad
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.text: Max, you look happy. Did you enjoy the festival?

transcript.speaker: Max
transcript.text: Oh yes, it was Thanksgiving. I went home to celebrate with my family.

transcript.speaker: Song Lin
transcript.text: Wonderful! What did your mother cook?

transcript.speaker: Max
transcript.text: A big roast turkey, mashed potatoes, pumpkin pie and apple pie.

transcript.speaker: Song Lin
transcript.text: That sounds delicious. What did you do after dinner?

transcript.speaker: Max
transcript.text: We watched a sports game on TV and shared what we were grateful for.

transcript.speaker: Song Lin
transcript.text: And what was the best part of the festival for you?

transcript.speaker: Max
transcript.text: Honestly, just being together with everyone I love.

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 Enjoying Festivals Politely
exercises.speaker: uk_female
exercises.transcript: Here is some simple advice for anyone visiting a festival in another country. First, learn a little about the festival's customs before you go, so you understand what is happening. Second, dress in a way that fits the occasion; at some ceremonies people wear traditional costumes. Third, always show respect for local traditions, even if they seem strange to you. If you are not sure what to do, just watch the people around you and follow them politely. Remember that every custom has a meaning behind it. By joining in with an open heart, you will not only enjoy the festival more, but also make new friends and feel truly welcome.
exercises.translation_cn: 给到外国参加节日的人一些简单建议:第一,去之前先了解一点节日习俗,以便明白正在发生什么;第二,穿着要合乎场合,有些仪式上人们会穿传统服装;第三,即使某些传统看起来奇怪,也要始终尊重当地传统;若不确定该怎么做,就观察周围的人并礼貌地跟着做;记住每个习俗背后都有含义;以开放的心态参与,你不仅会更享受节日,还会结交新朋友、感到真正受欢迎。
